speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, how many episodes have you had in the last 24 hours, and have there been any episodes of vomiting?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history; the combination of recent levofloxacin use and nine episodes of watery diarrhea in 48 hours strongly suggests *Clostridioides difficile* infection. Have you noticed any fever, or have you experienced blood or pus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: *Clostridioides difficile* infection (CDI). I have gathered sufficient clinical information from your history of recent levofloxacin use and high-volume watery diarrhea to confirm this diagnosis; please continue with appropriate antibiotic management.
